why: The biomes are the atlas's catalog, not a ladder of literals: `display-packages/biomes/package.shspec` carries the climate envelopes that partition the climate plane, the classified types that express an envelope on the ground a column has (its water and its terrain position), and §15b's hydrology overlays. The rows below are the package's own, in the package's own order, and `biome_library::tests::the_record_and_the_library_name_the_same_rows_in_the_same_order` fails if this record and the mounted catalog disagree. The library embeds the package and the game mounts the folder at boot, so the catalog is the file on disk rather than a table in Rust; a row the ground's own laws cannot produce, or that no reading tells apart from an earlier row, is deferred in that same package with the field it waits on. The measured rows after the catalog are the picture it draws on the default world at the map's own 32 m cells: the atlas's premise is that climate sets the envelope and terrain redistributes it, so a sheet where neighbouring cells of one climate change formation every cell is not a catalog but noise. Before the landform baseline below, the mountain, forest and tundra sheets over 900 m changed formation between neighbouring cells 26 %, 29 % and 58 % of the time, with precipitation spanning 32 … 1 812 mm in 900 m — the upslope was read two metres apart, which is a point sample of the ridged term's finest octaves rather than a mountain.
recipe: cargo run -p voxel-shapers --example biome-sheet-probe (seed GAME_SEED 2468, Config::default(), 28 x 32 declared cells of 32 m at the three camera centres the map window's screenshots named: (6824, -27426) the mountain view, (1416, -46452) the forest view, (2446, -48808) the tundra view; each cell classified the way `ecology::biome_at` classifies it, tick 0; the mosaic rows count neighbouring cells whose formation differs, out of 1 732 neighbouring pairs a sheet; `-- library` prints the catalog rows block from the mounted package)
measured: 2026-10-27, the pass that made the biomes a mounted catalog; the landform-step measurements reproduce unchanged from the pass that added them

rows.name: precipitation span over 900 m, mountain sheet
rows.note: 36 … 733 mm, against 32 … 1 812 mm before. The forest sheet reads 26 … 839 mm (was 30 … 1 838) and the tundra sheet 12 … 1 410 mm (was 13 … 6 452). A rain shadow still spans the atlas's desert-to-forest range — a range does that — but it now does so once per range instead of once per cell.

rows.name: rows in the mounted catalog
rows.note: 16 envelopes, 19 classified types, 3 §15b overlays and 12 deferred rows with their reasons. Every classified row names the atlas section it was read from (`biome_library::tests::every_row_names_the_atlas_section_it_was_read_from`), and this record carries every row, with its role, in the package's order.

rows.name: classified types reachable by the generator
rows.note: `every_type_is_reachable_and_stands_in_its_own_envelope` asks each type for its own envelope, water and position and requires the classifier to produce it from a column the ground laws allow — saturation is flat, a ridge is steep or high, and a belt is above the montane line. A row nothing can generate is a label no column can ever be given.

rows.name: overlays reachable by the generator
rows.note: `every_overlay_is_reachable` asks for each overlay's water and position and requires the classifier to answer with it. The two peat rows share the marsh's flat and are deferred by `no field tells them apart`; the wet slope is deferred because the ground's own laws cannot produce it.

rows.name: the package's envelope rows against the ladder it replaced
rows.note: `the_envelope_rows_are_the_ladder_it_replaced` sweeps 8 500 climates from -40 … 45 C and 0 … 2 500 mm and requires the package's envelope to answer exactly what `ecology::biome_for` answered before the catalog landed — the classification changed vocabulary, not behaviour.

rows.name: the package and the embedded copy are the same bytes
rows.note: `the_package_is_the_shipped_source` compares the crate's embedded copy with `display-packages/biomes/package.shspec`: the shipped catalog and the folder are one declaration, so a build cannot classify from a package that is not on disk.

rows.name: the built game classifies from the mounted package
rows.note: At boot `crates/shploingus/src/main.rs` mounts this folder's `package.shspec` and prints the catalog it adopted (`50 rows (16 envelopes, 19 types, 3 overlays, 12 deferred) from biomes v1`) and the spawn column's climate. With the same binary and only the montane tundra row's `biome` edited on disk to `desert`, the same boot line read `the montane_tundra envelope, formation desert` instead of `formation tundra`; the file was restored byte-identically and no rebuild was made between the runs. The world's materials, flora and map reach `ecology::biome_for`, which reads this catalog.

rows.name: the upslope baseline, in engine metres
rows.note: One wavelength of the ridged mountain term (`terrain::range_wavelength_m`, 1 / (continent_frequency * 6)) — 533 real metres at the world's 1/8 scale, which is the scale of the landform the air climbs.

unstable.name: the climate belt's own wavelength
unstable.note: The temperature belt varies at `continent_frequency`, about 400 engine metres, so a sheet 900 m across crosses two belts and the biomes of *any* classifier change every few hundred metres. The atlas's premise is the reverse — climate sets a region, terrain varies inside it — so the belt wants the same landform-scale treatment the upslope just got, and the tundra sheet's remaining 27 % is where that shows. Named owed, not done: it moves every biome in the world, and it is a climate model change rather than a library one.

unstable.name: the deferred §15 rows
unstable.note: Twelve catalogued rows are declared but not classified. Nine have no field to read them from (salinity, flow accumulation, flood recurrence, tide, distance to the sea, standing water, groundwater discharge); the two peat overlays share the marsh's water and flat and wait on a chemistry that tells them apart; and the temperate rain forest's wet slope waits on run-off, because saturation and slope cannot both read. They are rows of the same package, and `every_deferred_row_names_what_it_waits_on_and_is_not_in_the_tables` refuses a deferred row that has quietly joined the catalog.
